walkthroughs.body_html:
Conflict & Tension 1918-1939 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Conflict & Tension 1918-1939 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Conflict & Tension 1918-1939.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who led reformist Czechoslovakia during Prague Spring?
options: Tito
Dubcek
Nagy
Walesa

mcqs.q: When was the Berlin Wall built?
Why did British women get the vote in 1918?
options: A combination of pre-war suffragist and suffragette campaigning, women's contribution to WWI, and broader political changes including extending male suffrage.
Emmeline Pankhurst was elected to Parliament and voted it through.
Women got the vote as a reward for their work in WWI.
Vesalius invented the microscope.

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: Vesalius invented the microscope.
He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.

mcqs.q: Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
Emmeline Pankhurst was elected to Parliament and voted it through.
